walkthroughs.body_html:
Numerical Methods — a core area of A-Level Maths.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Numerical Methods brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Numerical Methods.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Using Newton-Raphson on f(x) = x² − 2 with x₀ = 1.5, what is x₁? (Give to 3 dp.)
The trapezium rule estimates which kind of quantity?
options: a definite integral
a derivative
a sum to infinity
a stationary point

mcqs.q: What is the range of the data set [4, 7, 2, 9, 5]?
options: 6, by multiplying -3 by 2.
From 2 to 9 — the range is given as two values.
7 — the largest minus the smallest (9 - 2).
5, because that is the middle value.
6, by multiplying -3 by 2.
-9 — without brackets, the exponent applies only to the 3, then the negative is applied: -(3^2) = -9.
5, because that is the middle value.
9, because squaring a negative number always gives a positive.

mcqs.q: If a data set has an extreme outlier, which average is most affected?
options: 5, because that is the middle value.
The mean — because every value (including the outlier) contributes to it.
The mode is most affected because the outlier becomes the new most common value.
The median is most affected because the outlier shifts the middle.
